audits.summary: All four claimed gates substantially hold on this working tree: Property vitest 706/706 passed (23 files), web-shared 326/326 passed (13 files), Property tsc --noEmit exit 0, HEAD = f90e029b with zero uncommitted changes under Property/web, packages/web-shared, supabase/, or docs/property (the 235 dirty paths are all generalist/optimisation_engine/scratch). One gate is overstated: web-shared has no tsconfig at all, so 'tsc clean both' has no runnable definition there; a standalone strict check shows 4 test-file-only type errors (production source clean). Test QUALITY is strong at the lib level (opt-out irreversibility, promotion idempotency, cron claim/retry semantics, DST/quiet-hours all genuinely asserted) but thin at the route level: of ~14 lead/cron routes only inbound/email and events are handler-tested. Top untested seams, in order: (1) the 289-line /api/leads/submit chokepoint, (2) the Twilio SMS webhook including its hand-rolled signature verification (the sole SMS path to 'contactable'), (3) the DB kill-switch lib + cron auth/arming wiring, (4) the guardrail/digest alert-dispatch async layer (explicitly excluded by the tests' own header), (5) the playground 'scenario suite' which asserts almost nothing. No failing tests, no count mismatches; findings are coverage-quality, not gate-falsity, except the minor web-shared tsc claim.

confirmed.title: POST /api/leads/submit (the server chokepoint) has zero route-level tests
confirmed.claim: The single most critical seam in the system, the submit route that saves/dedupes/verifies/enrols every lead and fires the instant touch, is never imported by any test. Only its leaf dependencies (verifyLead, processLeadStep, tokens, send-window) are unit-tested.
confirmed.evidence: grep across Property/web/src/tests for route imports finds exactly two route handlers under test: inbound-email.test.ts:101 imports @/app/api/leads/inbound/email/route and lead-events.test.ts:53 imports @/app/api/leads/events/route. No test imports leads/submit/route. The route contains ~240 lines of untested orchestration: honeypot flag-store (lines 98-108), validation thresholds (line 111: digits(phone)<10, message<10), email-only dedupe + update path (118-162), enrol-once via ignoreDuplicates + status 'new'->'nurturing' transition (220-234), isTest->live:!isTest sender flag (236), ctx.inSmsWindow synchronous step-1 fire (245-247), after() AI copy dispatch (252-265).
confirmed.impact: A regression anywhere in this wiring (e.g. the dedupe update clobbering fields, ignoreDuplicates behaviour change, validation rejecting real leads, honeypot branch failing) would lose or block real leads at the only entry point, and the suite would stay green. This site already had one silent lead-capture outage (2026-06-24) and a honeypot silent-drop bug found only by live probing.

verdicts.reasoning: Verified true. Repo-wide grep confirms no test anywhere imports Property/web/src/app/api/leads/submit/route.ts; vitest include is src/**/*.test.ts and the only route handlers under test are inbound/email and events, exactly as the auditor found. The route is 289 lines and every cited untested construct sits at the cited lines (honeypot store 98-108, validation 111, dedupe 118-162, ignoreDuplicates enrol 220-231, status flip 234, live:!isTest 236, inSmsWindow step-1 245-247, after() dispatch 252-265). Leaf coverage is even slightly thinner than claimed (only computePass is tested, not verifyLead). Route testing is feasible here — two sibling routes are tested with the same mocked-admin pattern. However, severity corrects DOWN from high to medium: this is a coverage gap, not an active defect, and the impact claim ignores three compensating guards verified in code: (1) submit-client.ts surfaces any route failure as a visible form error (a hard regression is not silent), (2) operator heads-up fires from DB AFTER INSERT triggers independent of the route's post-save orchestration, so any saved lead still reaches the operator, (3) scripts/lead_nurture_probe.mjs provides a live post-deploy happy-path probe. The genuinely silent regression surface is narrower than 'lose real leads at the only entry point': the honeypot branch (returns success:true even if its insert throws — and it is the fix for the previously confirmed silent-drop bug), the dedupe update clobber, the enrol-once ignoreDuplicates contract (regression could double-fire step 0/1 to real people), and the live:!isTest flag. On a live, armed system with two prior incidents at this seam, that residual risk makes this a solid medium: worth fixing promptly, but not a present high-severity exposure.

Technical claim verified exactly. Property/web/src/app/api/leads/submit/route.ts (289 lines) contains all cited logic at the cited line numbers (honeypot store 98-108, validation 111, email-only dedupe+update 118-162, enrol-once ignoreDuplicates 220-234, live:!isTest 236, sync step-1 fire 245-247, after() AI dispatch 252-265), and grep across Property/web and packages/web-shared confirms NO test imports or exercises this route. Only two route handlers have route-level tests (inbound/email at inbound-email.test.ts:101, events at lead-events.test.ts:53), which proves the NextRequest+mocked-admin test pattern already exists in-repo and was simply not applied to the most critical route. Leaf coverage is even slightly thinner than claimed: only the pure computePass from verify.ts is tested, not verifyLead itself. All phone-bearing leads (LeadForm + MiniCapture, the primary conversion path) flow through this route via submit-client.ts. However, the real-world impact is overstated, so severity downgrades high -> medium: (1) the route's fail-safe architecture means most of the untested ~240 lines (verify, enrol, instant touch, AI dispatch, booking token) are try/catch best-effort whose regression degrades nurture but does not lose the lead; the truly silent-loss surface is narrow (honeypot-branch best-effort insert that still returns success:true on failure, and dedupe misattribution) while validation/insert regressions return user-visible 400/500s; (2) an unmentioned operational mitigation exists: scripts/lead_nurture_probe.mjs, a non-polluting synthetic probe that POSTs a source='test' lead to the real deployed route and asserts save+verify+enrol, covering the happy path end-to-end against real infra (deploy-time/manual only, no branch coverage, not a CI net); (3) observability (daily digest cron, vw_lead_nurture_health, console panel) bounds a silent regression to roughly 1-2 days ~= 1-3 lost leads (£85-255 direct plus DJH-relationship damage) at Property volume; (4) both historical incidents cited as evidence (2026-06-24 env-var corruption outage, honeypot autofill drop) were environmental/client-side failures that route-level vitest would NOT have caught, so the "this already happened here" argument proves the risk class but not that these tests would have prevented them. The gap is real and worth closing cheaply (the pattern exists in lead-events.test.ts) because the system is live, armed, and under active development with pending changes adjacent to this route, but it is a coverage/robustness gap with partial mitigations and bounded blast radius, not a defect: medium, not high.

confirmed.title: Twilio inbound webhook (SMS/WhatsApp replies) completely untested, including the hand-rolled signature verification
confirmed.claim: The webhook that captures the responses which drive the entire contactability gate has no tests: not the custom HMAC-SHA1 verifyTwilioSignature (implemented without the Twilio SDK), not the proxy-aware URL reconstruction (x-forwarded-proto/host, port-stripping), not STOP keyword opt-out routing, not the resolveLeadId phone->lead fallback (last-9-digit ilike).
confirmed.evidence: grep -rln 'twilio' Property/web/src/tests/ matches only lead-nurture.playground.test.ts (which mocks channels, does not exercise the route). verifyTwilioSignature (route lines 36-57) and the URL reconstruction (127-144) are module-private and reachable only through the untested POST handler. The code comment at line 137-139 ('Force-strip any port so a forwarded ":443"... cannot break the HMAC match and 403 every real reply') shows this exact seam has already bitten once.
confirmed.impact: A bug here 403s or mis-attributes every inbound SMS/WhatsApp reply. Since contactable requires responded AND phone proven, and SMS reply is the primary phone proof, a silent regression means no lead can ever be promoted via SMS: they all age into 'unreachable' and are never forwarded to DJH, with nothing failing in CI. Downstream libs (stopNurture, recordResponseAndEvaluate, acknowledgeReply) are tested, but the signature/parsing/dispatch layer in front of them is not.

verdicts.reasoning: Verified every factual claim independently. The route (Property/web/src/app/api/leads/inbound/twilio/route.ts, exactly 229 lines) contains the hand-rolled HMAC-SHA1 verifyTwilioSignature (lines 36-57), the proxy-aware URL reconstruction with the port-stripping comment proving this seam already 403'd real replies once (lines 127-144), the last-9-digit ilike resolveLeadId fallback (90-101), and STOP keyword routing (179-182) — all module-private, reachable only via POST. Repo-wide grep for inbound/twilio|verifyTwilioSignature|x-twilio-signature matches only the route and two docs: zero tests. Crucially, this is not house style — the codebase already route-tests webhooks at exactly this level (lead-events.test.ts imports the events route POST and tests Svix HMAC accept + 401-on-invalid; inbound-email.test.ts imports the email inbound route POST), so the Twilio route is a conspicuous omission with the harness pattern ready. Downstream libs (stopNurture, toE164UK, recordResponseAndEvaluate) are tested; the dispatch layer is not. The 'silent in CI' claim holds and extends to runtime: evaluateGuardrails in nurture-health.ts has no rule on inbound replies (only complaints/failed-sends/bounces/opt-outs/stuck), so a 403-ing webhook triggers nothing automated; replies_24h appears only in the human-read daily digest. Two corrections to impact that roughly cancel: (a) slight overstatement — booked/confirmed/email-reply still promote leads with non-bad Lookup phone_status, so the funnel degrades rather than zeroes; (b) missed aggravator — STOP opt-outs route exclusively through this webhook, so a regression silently drops opt-outs and email touches continue to leads who texted STOP (Twilio's default opt-out only backstops the SMS channel). Severity high stands: live armed production, sole entry for the only direct phone-proof event plus opt-out handling, hand-rolled crypto plus environment-dependent header reconstruction that has already broken once, silent failure mode, and only route-level tests can cover the private functions.

CONFIRMED with severity downgraded high->medium. The factual claims all verify: (1) zero test coverage — the only 'twilio' match under Property/web/src/tests/ is lead-nurture.playground.test.ts whose sole mention is a comment about simulating Twilio Lookup; nothing imports the route; verifyTwilioSignature (route.ts:36-57) and the proxy URL reconstruction (127-144) are module-private and reachable only through the untested POST handler. (2) The route is a genuine outlier: sibling inbound routes are 36-69-line thin wrappers over tested libs (lead-booking.test.ts, inbound-email.test.ts), while this one holds ~100 lines of security/protocol logic in the route module itself; downstream stopNurture/recordResponseAndEvaluate/acknowledgeReply ARE tested (34 refs, 4 test files). (3) The silence claim is if anything understated: evaluateGuardrails (nurture-health.ts:131-206) has NO rule on replies24h (only complaints/failed-sends/bounces/optouts/stuck), the daily digest self-suppresses on dormant days, and at single-digit monthly lead volume a reply drought is invisible; a 403ing webhook also drops STOP capture, so the 7-touch sequence keeps messaging opted-out leads (PECR exposure). However, the impact is overstated on two counts that pull severity down to medium: (a) SMS reply is NOT the only promotion path — contactability.ts:83-98 promotes on booked (/book signed token) or confirmed (email one-tap) or email reply whenever the phone is not known-bad, and those flows are thin routes over tested libs, so an inbound-webhook outage narrows the funnel rather than zeroing it ('they all age into unreachable' is wrong for any lead who books or taps the confirm link); (b) this is a missing-regression-protection gap, not a demonstrated defect — the HMAC implementation matches Twilio's documented scheme on inspection (URL + sorted key/value concat, HMAC-SHA1, base64, timing-safe compare), and the :443 comment shows the seam was already live-debugged and fixed, i.e. it currently works in production. Quantified real-world exposure: harm materialises only if a future code/platform change regresses the route; at Property's volume that would silently misroute roughly 1-2 leads/month into 'unreachable' (at £85/lead handoff value) plus unhonoured STOP opt-outs until someone notices the digest 'Replies: 0' line or Twilio console 403s. Real, worth fixing (extract the signature/URL/dispatch logic to a lib and pin it with tests, plus a synthetic signed-webhook probe), but a latent-risk coverage gap on currently-correct code with surviving alternate promotion paths is medium, not high.

confirmed.title: DB kill switch (nurture-control) and cron-route arming/auth wiring have no tests
confirmed.claim: isNurturePaused / the lead_nurture_control pause-resume lib is entirely untested (only a type import appears in any test), and the cron route's authorized() timing-safe bearer check plus the effectiveArmed = cronArmed && !dbPaused composition (route lines 58-70) are untested at route level. runLeadNurtureCron itself IS tested in web-shared, but only below this wiring.
confirmed.evidence: grep -rn 'nurture-control|isNurturePaused' Property/web/src/tests/ returns a single hit: nurture-digest.test.ts:13 'import type { NurtureControl }'. No test imports @/app/api/cron/lead-nurture/route. The custom padEnd(512) timingSafeEqual auth (route lines 32-45) and the 'guardrails still run while dbPaused' behaviour (lines 74-85) are asserted only in comments and docs.
confirmed.impact: The observability migration's headline safety feature, the DB kill switch, has no automated proof it actually halts sends. If isNurturePaused mis-parses the control row (or the route stops consulting it), pressing pause in the console would appear to work while the cron keeps messaging real leads. Conversely an auth regression would 401 Vercel Cron and silently stall all follow-up touches.

verdicts.reasoning: Every evidence point verified by direct inspection. (1) nurture-control.ts: the single test reference is 'import type { NurtureControl }' at Property/web/src/tests/nurture-digest.test.ts:13; no test exercises getNurtureControl/isNurturePaused/pauseNurture/resumeNurture/recordGuardrailAlert. (2) No test imports @/app/api/cron/lead-nurture/route; authorized() (lines 32-45), effectiveArmed = cronArmed && !dbPaused (lines 58-62), and guardrails-run-while-dbPaused (lines 74-85) match the finding and are untested. (3) runLeadNurtureCron IS tested in packages/web-shared/lead-nurture/lead-nurture.test.ts for both armed=false (no-op) and armed=true — the auditor scoped this correctly. (4) Route-level tests are an established repo pattern (inbound-email.test.ts, lead-events.test.ts import route handlers) and web-shared already mocks adminSelect, so no "the project never tests routes" refutation applies. (5) The gap is marginally broader than reported: the write side (console POST /api/nurture-control route and web-shared setNurturePaused, adminData.ts:1377) is also untested, so the entire pause chain has no automated coverage at any link except the pure evaluateGuardrails matrix (whose test header explicitly excludes runNurtureGuardrails). Severity stays medium, not higher, because: no current defect exists (writer/reader/migration schemas agree, PostgREST semantics correct, recordGuardrailAlert's merge-duplicates upsert correctly preserves paused); docs do not overclaim coverage; and the "silently stall" impact is partially overstated since the separate daily digest cron with its own authorized() copy would surface a stalled nurture cron via stuck-lead metrics within ~24h. It stays medium, not lower, because this is the headline safety control of a live, armed, real-send system whose deliberate fail-open design makes exactly the hypothesized regression (console shows paused, sends continue) silent, and closing the gap is cheap with existing harness patterns.

confirmed.title: Guardrail/alerting async layer (runNurtureGuardrails, getNurtureHealth) explicitly excluded from tests
confirmed.claim: Only the pure evaluateGuardrails threshold function is tested (42 tests). The impure layer that reads the health views, dispatches operator alert emails, and would perform the autopause write is deliberately untested, per the test file's own header.
confirmed.evidence: nurture-health.test.ts lines 2-5: 'Unit tests for the PURE evaluateGuardrails function... The async functions (getNurtureHealth, runNurtureGuardrails) are NOT tested'. Same pattern for the digest: composeDigestEmail has 45 tests but the /api/cron/lead-nurture-digest route (69 lines) has none.
confirmed.impact: Threshold logic is proven but the delivery of alerts is not: a broken view query, a failed alert email send, or a broken autopause write would go unnoticed by CI while the operator believes guardrails are watching an armed production system. This is adjacent to (but broader than) known-open item 1: alert-only posture is deliberate, alert-path untestedness is not stated anywhere.

verdicts.reasoning: Every factual element verified against the code. (1) nurture-health.ts is 377 lines; nurture-health.test.ts lines 4-6 state verbatim that getNurtureHealth and runNurtureGuardrails are NOT tested; exactly 42 it() cases, all on the pure evaluateGuardrails/DEFAULT_THRESHOLDS. (2) Grep across Property/web/src confirms no other test touches either async function; the sole caller api/cron/lead-nurture/route.ts has no tests, and no test references any cron route. (3) Digest mirror confirmed: composeDigestEmail has exactly 45 tests, gatherDigestData/runNurtureDigest untested per its own header, and the 69-line /api/cron/lead-nurture-digest route has zero coverage. (4) Docs (LEAD_NURTURE_OBSERVABILITY.md) cite 'Property vitest 706' as verification and mark only evaluateGuardrails '(unit-tested matrix)', never disclosing the untested alert path, so this is not a restatement of known-open item 1. The auditor actually understated one aspect: getNurtureHealth swallows all errors with a bare catch returning null and NO log line, and runNurtureGuardrails then returns an empty verdict, so a broken health view makes the guardrail layer silently inert with no signal anywhere (the daily digest's 'HEALTH DATA Not available' canary is suppressed on dormant days because health===null counts as no-activity). Mitigations keep this at medium rather than high: the pattern is deliberate and documented in test headers, the views were staging-applied and verified queryable at build, alert-send/autopause failures inside runNurtureGuardrails are console.error-logged, the cron route wraps the call in try/catch, and autopause is dormant (flag off) so the untested pause write is unreachable in prod today. It is an assurance gap, not a demonstrated defect, but on an armed production system where alert emails are the only active guardrail output, an untested delivery path with a by-design silent-blindness failure mode is correctly rated medium.

audits.summary: Entry path (form → /api/leads/submit → verify → save → enrol → step 0 → thank-you) is fundamentally well engineered and its prod wiring is genuinely live: fail-safe save-first ordering, fail-open verification, claim-before-send idempotency with cron retry, signed 14-day booking tokens, truthful dormancy-gated thank-you copy, honeypot de-fanged server-side, 706+326 tests green, routes/crons/env verified deployed and armed (no lead has traversed it yet — go-live was ~11:23 UTC today and the last lead arrived 08:55). Against that baseline I found two high-severity defects in exactly the paths the tests can't see: (1) the 24h dedupe update never writes phone/full_name, so the route's own \"check your number and submit again\" retry loop discards the corrected phone forever, and a prior email-only widget/resource row absorbs and strips a later fully-qualified submission; (2) a step whose channels all fail (any present-but-unroutable phone at the SMS step 1 — bot leads included, since verification doesn't gate enrolment) wedges the lead 'active' forever, kills its remaining email touches, and stuck rows sort first in the LIMIT-50 cron scan (starvation risk). Three live queries also reference lead_contact_events.created_at, a column that does not exist in prod (verified) — adminSelect swallows the 400s, silently disabling the documented hesitation/channel-shift reactivity, the booking_viewed once-per-day dedupe, and the complaint-alert throttle. Supporting issues: LEAD_RESEND_WEBHOOK_SECRET absent in prod (open/click/bounce/complaint capture dead), the armed unauthenticated chokepoint is an SMS-pumping/brand-spam vector with no rate limit or bot check, honeypot-caught humans get a false \"we just messaged you\" promise with no nurture, and the email-only surfaces bypass the whole contactability machine while retaining client-side honeypot drops.

confirmed.title: Dedupe path discards corrected phone (and name): the 'check it and submit again' UX cannot fix the stored number
confirmed.claim: When a submit dedupes onto an existing same-email lead (24h window), the update patch is only { message, role, submitted_at } — phone and full_name are never updated. But the route's own needsCheck UX explicitly tells a user whose phone verified 'invalid' to "check it and submit again"; that resubmit hits the dedupe path, so the corrected phone is written to lead_verification (upsert onConflict lead_id, submit/route.ts:171-186) but NEVER to leads.phone. Every SMS/WhatsApp nurture touch reads leads.phone (cron.ts:62, sendChannel send.ts:61), so all SMS goes to the old bad number forever. Same mechanism silently destroys data cross-surface: a ResourceGate/SpecialistWidget direct-insert row (full_name "", phone "") from the same email within 24h absorbs a later full qualified form submission, permanently losing the lead's name and phone from the lead row (emails greet "Hi there", all SMS steps skip).
confirmed.evidence: submit/route.ts:141: await adminUpdate("leads", { id: `eq.${leadId}` }, { message, role, submitted_at: baseRow.submitted_at }); — no phone/full_name. LeadForm.tsx:148: setFieldErrors({ phone: "That number does not look right. Please check it and submit again." }). Dedupe matches ANY same-source+email lead: submit/route.ts:126-133 (source eq, email eq, created_at gte 24h) — ResourceGate.tsx:120-136 and SpecialistWidget.tsx:343-366 insert rows with full_name:"", phone:"" into the same leads table with the same source. Handoff partially recovers via ver.phone_e164 || lead.phone (handoff.ts:118) but nurture sends and the console/lead row stay wrong.
confirmed.impact: A real human who does exactly what the form asks (fix their typo'd number and resubmit) still has the broken number on record: SMS touches fail or go to a stranger's number, and if their old number was 'invalid' the contactability gate later reads the NEW verification row (valid) while DJH-facing leads.phone is still the bad one. In the cross-surface case a fully qualified lead is degraded to an anonymous email-only record.

verdicts.reasoning: Every technical claim verified against the code. audits.summary: Audited the lead-nurture engine (packages/web-shared/lead-nurture/{config,tokens,send,cron}.ts), the hourly cron route, and lib/leads/{send-window,sequence-gen,aux-cron,nurture-control,nurture-health}.ts against the four LEAD_NURTURE_*.md docs, the two migrations, prod Vercel env/cron registration, and prod DB state (SELECT-only). The core machinery is solid and matches most claims: auth fails closed, env+db-pause gating order is correct, advance is properly status+step guarded, opt-out is non-resurrectable through every code writer of lead_nurture_state, the scheduler is genuinely DST-safe (verified empirically across both 2026/2027 transitions), the T0 split is deterministic FNV-1a, GENERATABLE_STEP_KEYS matches docs, and the claimed 706/326 green tests + clean Property tsc reproduce exactly. Prod is armed but has zero enrolments yet, so everything found is latent rather than an active incident. Three HIGH findings: (1) quiet hours are enforced only at schedule time — failed-send retries (hourly, 24/7) and pause/dormancy backlogs dispatch with no send-window re-check, so SMS can legally-riskily fire at 3am the moment a blocker clears (the aux scans check the window at dispatch; the main sequence does not); (2) test-lead isolation is broken in the cron path — the cron builds a live:true sender with no source filter, so an uncleaned source='test' probe gets real Twilio/Resend sends from step 2 onward (bouncing example.com emails into the deliverability guardrails), contradicting the probe's and channels.ts's written safety claims; (3) confirm and opt-out links execute full state changes on bare GETs with no human-proof, so email security scanners can silently close real leads (false opt-out, unbackstopped) or forge the 'responded' signal (false promotion + handoff). Mediums: pending-row takeover is at-least-once with no staleness gate (double-send on crash/lost-PATCH/concurrent runs, docs overstate 'no-op'); permanent channel failures retry hourly forever with no cap and never reach 'unreachable'; the failed_send_rate_1h pause rule is blind to retried failures because view windows key on claim-time sent_at that is never updated; the channel_shift deliverability pivot is unreachable (needs 3 prior emails, max is 2); and the real cadence runs ~a day slower than the documented table (vip_sameday is next-day for post-08:00 submits, and the empty VIP step costs every non-VIP lead an extra day). Lows/infos: channel-flag-off silently consumes steps mid-flight, batch-50 vs maxDuration=60s timeout risk after backlogs, a NULL-next_action_at blind spot shared by the cron and the stuck view, reply-ack lacking an opted_out check, and minor doc drift.

confirmed.title: No dispatch-time send-window check: overdue/retried steps can send SMS at any hour of night
confirmed.claim: Quiet hours are only enforced at SCHEDULE time (computeNextSendMs). The cron due-scan fires anything with next_action_at <= now, and processLeadStep/sendChannel never re-check inSendWindow at dispatch. Any row whose due time passed while the system was paused (db kill-switch), dormant (env flag), mid-Twilio-outage, or simply failing (all-failed steps are retried EVERY hourly tick, 24/7) will be dispatched at whatever hour the blocker clears, including 21:00-07:00 London.
confirmed.evidence: cron.ts:65 `next_action_at: lte.${nowIso}` with no window filter; send.ts sendChannel goes straight to sender.send (lines 98-109) with no inSendWindow call; grep confirms inSendWindow is only consulted in aux-cron.ts:317 and :413 and at submit (config/lead-nurture.ts:258). Concrete path: day1_sms fails at 20:00 tick (Twilio 5xx) -> status 'failed', state not advanced (send.ts:226) -> 21:00 tick takes over the failed row (send.ts:92-93) and re-sends at 21:00+ London, outside the documented 09:00-20:30 SMS window. Same for a db-pause resumed late evening: the whole backlog fires on the next tick.
confirmed.impact: PECR/annoyance-class violation the docs explicitly claim to prevent (PROGRAMME.md section 6 'quiet hours'). A landlord gets a chase SMS at 2-3am after an outage/pause recovery; complaints and opt-outs damage the exact deliverability signals the guardrails watch. The aux scans DO check the window at dispatch, showing the sequence path's omission is a gap, not a design choice.

verdicts.reasoning: Verified every element of the claim against the code. (1) The cron due-scan (packages/web-shared/lead-nurture/cron.ts:65) selects status=active rows with next_action_at <= now and no window filter. (2) processLeadStep/sendChannel (packages/web-shared/lead-nurture/send.ts) and the Property ChannelSender (Property/web/src/lib/leads/channels.ts) contain no inSendWindow check; the sender goes straight to Resend/Twilio after flag checks. Repo-wide grep confirms inSendWindow is consulted only at schedule time (config/lead-nurture.ts:615-622 computeNextSendMs), at submit for the instant step-1 SMS (submit/route.ts:245 via ctx.inSmsWindow, config/lead-nurture.ts:258; no step buildMessages reads it), and at dispatch in the aux scans only (aux-cron.ts:317, 413) — confirming the sequence-path omission is an inconsistency, not a design choice. (3) The retry path is real: send.ts:226 (shouldAdvance = failed===0 ? resolved>0 : sent>0) means an all-failed step never advances, and the hourly 24/7 cron (vercel.json "0 * * * *") takes over the failed claim (send.ts:92-93) and re-attempts at any hour; bestSendHour is clamped to max 20:00 so late-window sends exist, making a post-20:30 or overnight/Sunday retry send possible after provider failure. (4) DB-pause/dormancy backlog: route.ts:58-69 halts processing, due rows accumulate, and on resume the next tick fires up to 50 rows regardless of London hour; guardrails (nurture-health.ts) have no window/night detection, and autopause+resume would itself trigger an off-hours burst. (5) Docs explicitly promise quiet hours (LEAD_NURTURE_SYSTEM.md:98 "no SMS 21:00-09:00... Sun -> Mon"; PROGRAMME.md section 6), so code diverges from documented behaviour in a live, armed system. Severity corrected high -> medium: the happy scheduled path IS window-correct; violation requires a blocker clearing out-of-window. The likely manifestation is a send 30-90 minutes past the 20:30 close after a transient failure at a 20:00 tick; a 2-3am send needs a multi-hour outage or a late-night operator resume. Harm is bounded per lead by send idempotency (one overdue message per step, no repeats, batch cap 50), and the PECR framing overstates the legal exposure since these are solicited service follow-ups about the lead's own enquiry — the real risk is annoyance/complaints/opt-outs and deliverability signals. A one-line dispatch-time inSendWindow check with reschedule-to-next-window-open would close the gap.

Confirmed in code on every point. The due scan (packages/web-shared/lead-nurture/cron.ts:60-68) is status=active AND next_action_at<=now with no window filter; processLeadStep/sendChannel (send.ts) and the channel sender (Property/web/src/lib/leads/channels.ts) contain zero time awareness; the cron runs 0 * * * * (24/7, Property/web/vercel.json). inSendWindow is only consulted at schedule time (config/lead-nurture.ts:258, :616) and, tellingly, at dispatch time in the aux scans (aux-cron.ts:317, :413) — proving the sequence path's omission is a gap, not a design choice. The retry amplifier is real: send.ts:226 refuses to advance an all-failed step, and send.ts:92-93 takes over the failed row every hourly tick, so an SMS blocked by a Twilio outage sends at whatever hour recovery lands, including overnight. The pause amplifier is real: resumeNurture (nurture-control.ts) only flips paused=false, nothing reschedules stale next_action_at and no janitor exists, so a backlog fires on the first tick after resume at any hour; the DB kill switch (the designated incident tool) thus guarantees an out-of-window replay if resumed after 20:30. Docs (LEAD_NURTURE_PROGRAMME.md section 6) present the 09:00-20:30 SMS window as a system property and never document backlog replay, so this contradicts claimed behaviour. However, severity 'high' overstates real-world impact: (1) normal operation never triggers it — computeNextSendMs schedules everything in-window (max hour 20:00); it needs an abnormal event (multi-hour provider outage spanning past 20:30, evening pause-resume, re-arm, cron outage), realistically a few times per year; (2) blast radius per event is a handful of leads (Property's active pipeline is small; 5 of 8 steps carry SMS) receiving ONE step's messages at a bad hour, after which the min-gap guard re-spaces subsequent steps in-window — no repeated night spam, no data or lead loss; (3) a 21:00-23:00 send (evening resume) is far more likely than the headline 2-3am case, which requires an outage recovering overnight since no operator resumes at 3am, and the console pause panel is not even deployed yet (known-open item 3) and autopause is off, so pause/resume frequency is currently low; (4) the 'PECR violation' framing is legally overstated — PECR/Ofcom statutory quiet-hours restrictions cover live marketing calls, not SMS; SMS timing is ICO/DMA good practice, so the harm class is annoyance/opt-outs/complaints plus contradiction of the system's own documented posture, not regulatory breach. Real bug, cheap fix (one inSendWindow check at dispatch with reschedule to next window open), bounded conditional impact: medium.

verdicts.reasoning: Confirmed by direct code inspection. The cron route (Property/web/src/app/api/cron/lead-nurture/route.ts:56) builds one sender with { live: true } for the whole batch; the shared cron (packages/web-shared/lead-nurture/cron.ts:61-95) selects leads.source but never filters or uses it; sendChannel/processLeadStep (send.ts) have no source check and skips count as resolved so live:false steps 0/1 advance the state (send.ts:226). Severity corrected down from high to medium: real documented-invariant violation on a live armed system with a plausible routine trigger (future prod probes are planned), but currently latent, the documented go-live probe ran while dormant (no enrolment when unarmed), standard probe values reach only an Ofcom-reserved number and example.com (no real person is messaged), the sequence self-terminates, and guardrail alerts would surface the bounces. confirmed.title: Pending-row takeover creates real double-send windows (at-least-once, and no staleness gate against concurrent runs)
confirmed.claim: The claim-before-send design is at-least-once, not exactly-once: (a) if the function crashes or the status PATCH fails between a successful provider send (line 99-109) and the 'sent' update (line 122-126), the row stays 'pending' and the next tick takes it over and re-sends the same message; (b) the takeover has no staleness threshold, so two CONCURRENT invocations (scheduled tick + a manual POST, both GET and POST are exposed) both treat the other's fresh 'pending' claim as a crashed attempt and both send.
confirmed.evidence: send.ts:80-93: on conflict, any non-terminal status ('pending'/'failed') is taken over immediately (`sendRowId = row.id; // take over a pending/failed claim`) with no check of how old the claim is. Migration 20260701000001 comments and LEAD_NURTURE_SYSTEM.md:43 describe the unique claim as making 'a retry/overlap ... a no-op', which is only true for terminal rows.
confirmed.impact: A lead can receive the same email/SMS twice after a mid-flight crash, a lost PATCH to Supabase, or overlapping cron invocations. Low probability per event but the docs overstate the guarantee; the standard fix (claimed_at timestamp + only take over claims older than N minutes) is absent.

verdicts.reasoning: Confirmed by direct code inspection. (a) At-least-once is real: in packages/web-shared/lead-nurture/send.ts the provider send (line 99) precedes the 'sent' PATCH (line 122) with no atomicity; a hard kill between them leaves a 'pending' row and un-advanced state, and the next hourly tick takes the row over (line 93) and re-sends. A PATCH that throws marks the row 'failed' (lines 128-135) despite actual delivery — also non-terminal, also re-sent next tick. One nuance the finding overstates: adminUpdate (packages/web-shared/nurture/admin.ts) never throws on HTTP non-ok and its result is ignored, so a merely-failed 'sent' PATCH still returns "sent" and advances lead_nurture_state — that sub-path yields an orphaned pending row, not a re-send, unless the advance PATCH also fails. (b) No staleness gate confirmed: takeover is unconditional for any non-terminal row; no claimed_at column or age check exists anywhere in the package or migration 20260701000001. Real concurrency vectors: submit route fires step 0/1 synchronously right after inserting state with next_action_at=now, so an hourly cron tick landing in that seconds-wide window double-fires the same step with no operator involvement; a manual CRON_SECRET-authed GET/POST can also overlap the scheduled tick. Mitigating fact: the scheduled cron cannot overlap itself (hourly schedule, maxDuration=60s). Docs overstatement confirmed verbatim: migration line 91 says "a retry/overlap is a no-op", untrue for non-terminal rows/concurrent overlap. Severity corrected medium -> low: the at-least-once posture is an explicit, documented design choice in the send.ts header (takeover exists to close the silent-drop "ghost sent" window, a defensible trade for lead nurture); worst-case impact is one duplicate email/SMS to a lead already in a 7-touch sequence (no lead loss, no data loss, no security issue); expected frequency at current volume (a few leads/week, ms-wide crash windows, seconds-wide overlap windows once per hour) is roughly <=1 event/year. Legitimate hardening item (add claimed_at + takeover age threshold; fix the migration comment), not a medium-risk defect.

confirmed.title: Permanently failing channels retry hourly forever: no retry cap, no terminal state, lead never becomes 'unreachable'
confirmed.claim: When a step's channels produce failures and zero sends, the state is deliberately not advanced so the next tick retries, but there is no cap or backoff: a PERMANENT failure (unparseable phone -> sendSms returns null; TWILIO_SMS_FROM unset; Twilio number-blocked after a carrier-level STOP that missed the webhook) retries every hour indefinitely, inserting a send_failed lead_contact_event each hour, and the lead is frozen mid-sequence forever instead of reaching 'unreachable'.

Submit validation only requires >=10 digits (submit/route.ts:111), so a 15+ digit junk phone passes validation but never normalises (toE164UK returns null).
confirmed.impact: Provider attempts and event-table spam every hour per stuck lead until an operator manually intervenes; a day1_sms-stuck lead never receives the remaining email touches either (whole sequence frozen). Severity: medium is honest. Real correctness defect in a live armed system, deterministic freeze from realistic user input, no self-healing, guardrail metrics partially blinded, manual SQL-level intervention needed to un-stick; but bounded by daily-digest detection within ~24h, intact inbound conversion, low lead volume (likely 0-2 affected at a time), and modest resource churn. Not high (no data loss, no wrong messages sent to humans, detection exists), not low (defeats the system's core purpose for affected leads with no terminal state or cap).

audits.summary: Audited the inbound half of the live Property lead-nurture system (Twilio webhook, email inbound, booking, contactability gate, dossier/handoff, aux-cron, observability migrations) read-only at HEAD f90e029b. Three high findings: (1) the one-tap confirm link performs promotion + DJH handoff on a bare GET, so corporate email link scanners can fabricate 'contactable' leads — the exact failure mode the system exists to prevent; (2) the GET opt-out footer link opts leads out with no confirmation step, so the same scanners silently kill real leads (invisible lead loss); (3) leads.status is never written to 'unreachable' or 'forwarded' by any code despite docs claiming '(now actually written)' — the funnel view, health view, daily digest and the console's unreachable panel will read 0/empty forever, blinding the owner's 3-of-9 success metric. Mediums: natural-language opt-outs by SMS ('please stop', 'not interested') are treated as qualifying replies and promoted with a 'we'll call you' auto-ack; the handoff email has no retry and records 'handed_off' before attempting the send (a Resend blip permanently loses a qualified lead); inbound phone->lead resolution is unordered when leads share a number (replies/STOPs credited to the wrong row); the documented AI 'DJH call brief' is dead code never wired into handoff.ts; and scanner GETs of /book trigger the abandoned-booking SMS nudge. Lows/infos cover the opted-out-lead-rebooks false promise, infinite hourly retries for permanently-failing sends (a lead that can never reach 'unreachable'), the unconditional 'Contact details verified.' banner when phone_status is unknown, and minor races/validation edges.

verdicts.reasoning: Every technical element of the finding verifies against the code. GET /api/leads/confirm/[token] (Property/web/src/app/api/leads/confirm/[token]/route.ts:29) runs recordResponseAndEvaluate("confirmed","email") on a bare GET with only HMAC token validation — no interstitial, no POST, no bot/user-agent heuristic anywhere in the chain (route, middleware.ts matcher covers only /blog and /locations, vercel.json has no firewall rules, no click-timing filter in web-shared/lead-nurture/send.ts). contactability.ts:89-91 promotes on confirmed && !phoneKnownBad, where phoneKnownBad is only 'invalid'/'voip', so unknown/null phone passes; promotion flips leads.status to 'contactable', fires the operator handoff email, and also cancels the remaining nurture sequence. Corporate link-scanning products (Proofpoint, Mimecast, Defender pre-delivery detonation) fetching email links via GET is a well-documented real-world failure mode — it is exactly why RFC 8058 mandates POST for one-click unsubscribe, and tellingly the sibling optout route DOES implement RFC 8058 POST while the confirm path does not (and the optout GET footer link is a sibling exposure that would silently close a lead). tokens.ts:12 explicitly encodes the broken assumption ("The confirm link proves a human acted"). The manual operator review does not mitigate: the dossier shows "confirmed by one-tap link" but a scanner fetch is indistinguishable from a genuine click. Severity high is correct (not critical): it defeats the system's central contactability gate in live, armed production with a direct £85/dud-lead financial and reputation path, plus silent nurture cancellation and contamination of contactability/T0-experiment metrics; but it is bounded per incident, affects only the link-scanning-mailbox segment, causes no data loss or security breach, and a human forward step still exists. Impact is marginally worse than filed: the false promote also kills the remaining 7-touch chase for a lead who never actually engaged.

Confirmed real; severity high stands. Every cited line verifies: confirm/[token]/route.ts:29 runs recordResponseAndEvaluate("confirmed","email") on a bare GET (Next.js also maps HEAD to this GET), contactability.ts:89-91 promotes on confirmed when phone_status is not invalid/voip (unknown passes), the confirm link is in every branded nurture email as the secondary CTA (lead-nurture.ts:174/314) with a 14-day token (tokens.ts:47), and no bot/interstitial/UA defence exists anywhere (middleware only matches /blog and /locations; BotID deliberately unwired per api/track comment; no guardrail watches confirm latency). Scanner-driven GETs from secure email gateways are a well-established failure mode (the same reason magic-link auth breaks), and the codebase itself acknowledges machine clicks by implementing RFC 8058 POST on the opt-out route while leaving confirm as a state-mutating GET. The finding is actually slightly WORSE than reported: dossier.ts:77-85 awards +1 for the one-tap confirm plus +1 for "Responded within an hour of enquiring", so a scanner fetch seconds after the instant step-0 email raises the readiness score, and handoff.ts:185 headlines "Actively responded and ready for a call" - the sole mitigation (manual operator review) is actively misled, not neutral. Promotion also nulls next_action_at, permanently killing the lead's remaining 7-touch sequence, and corrupts the T0 experiment and nurture health metrics the system is being evaluated on right now. Real-world quantification keeps this at high rather than critical: lead flow is small (~10-25/month), the exposed segment is corporate/scanned mailboxes (likely 10-25% of landlord leads, only a fraction of whose gateways fetch at delivery), so expect roughly 1-3 false promotions/month; and a falsely promoted lead is still a genuine enquirer with a submit-time Twilio-verified phone, so each event is quality-bar dilution (the exact pre-system 3-of-9 problem, plus a possible wrongful GBP 85 charge on the 10-day-old DJH agreement) rather than a fabricated lead. Silent, undetectable corruption of the system's single core guarantee on a live armed production path, with a trivial fix (interstitial page with a POST button), is a textbook high.

confirmed.title: Inbound SMS lead resolution is non-deterministic when two leads share a phone number, and an opt-out can be applied to the wrong lead row
confirmed.claim: The primary lookup (lead_verification.phone_e164 eq, limit 1) has NO order clause, so when the same person re-submits after the 24h dedupe window (or a household shares a number) PostgREST returns an arbitrary row — typically the OLDEST lead. A reply or STOP is then credited to that stale lead: the reply promotes an already-contactable/closed row (alreadyPromoted no-op) while the newer lead's nurture sequence keeps texting the same phone to exhaustion; a STOP stops only the arbitrary matched lead's sequence, leaving the other lead's state 'active'. The fallback path (leads.phone ilike last-9-digits, order created_at.desc) inconsistently picks the NEWEST, and misses stored phones with internal spaces (e.g. '07700 900123' does not contain the contiguous '700900123').
confirmed.evidence: twilio/route.ts:81-85: `adminSelect("lead_verification", { select: "lead_id", phone_e164: eq..., limit: "1" })` — no order param. Dedupe only spans 24h and only same-email (submit/route.ts:125-133), so duplicate-phone leads are expected over time.
confirmed.impact: Replies stop the wrong chase (lead keeps getting SMS after replying — the exact annoyance the system exists to prevent), and for non-exact-STOP opt-outs (finding INBOUND-4) the person can keep receiving messages from the sibling lead row. Exact STOP is backstopped by Twilio's provider-level per-number block, but our own state stays inconsistent.

verdicts.reasoning: Confirmed by direct code inspection; no hidden guard exists anywhere in the call chain. (1) resolveLeadId primary lookup (Property/web/src/app/api/leads/inbound/twilio/route.ts:81-85) is phone_e164 eq + limit 1 with NO order — arbitrary row under PostgREST when multiple leads share a phone. (2) Duplicate-phone rows are expected: lead_verification is 1:1 with leads (PK lead_id, migration 20260701000001) with no uniqueness on phone_e164; submit dedupe (submit/route.ts:125-133) is same-email+source within 24h only, and toE164UK normalizes formatting so both duplicates match the inbound From exactly. Worse, a >24h resubmit also creates a SECOND ACTIVE lead_nurture_state enrolment (onConflict lead_id,sequence with a new lead_id), so two parallel sequences to one phone is the natural precondition. (3) recordResponseAndEvaluate/promoteIfContactable/stopNurture (lib/leads/contactability.ts) act only on the single resolved lead_id, and the cron (packages/web-shared/lead-nurture/cron.ts) chases every active state row independently — grep confirms there is no phone-level suppression anywhere. A reply thus stops one arbitrary row while the sibling keeps texting/emailing the person who just replied; a STOP applied to the wrong row leaves the sibling active (Twilio provider block covers SMS only; sibling emails continue, and the opted_out event sits on the wrong lead — inconsistent compliance state). (4) Fallback claims verified: ilike '%last9' suffix match misses '07700 900123' (space breaks contiguity) and orders created_at.desc (newest), inconsistent with the primary. Severity stays medium: live in production and defeats the system's core anti-goal (chasing a lead who replied) plus wrong-row opt-out records, but occurrence requires the duplicate-phone precondition at low lead volume, Twilio backstops the SMS STOP channel, and no lead data is lost.

Every factual pillar of the finding verified correct under independent inspection, but the open question it flagged is now positively resolved in the benign direction, so severity drops from medium to info.

What I confirmed (all auditor claims accurate): (a) An idle cron run writes nothing to the DB by design — verified in C:\Users\user\Documents\Accounting\Property\web\src\app\api\cron\lead-nurture\route.ts, packages\web-shared\lead-nurture\cron.ts (early return {processed:0} when no due rows, no writes), and Property\web\src\lib\leads\nurture-health.ts (only writes recordGuardrailAlert after a successful breach alert email). (c) 'vercel crons ls' confirms 3 crons incl. /api/cron/lead-nurture '0 * * * *'. (d) I also checked the worse scenario the auditor could have missed: CRON_SECRET and LEAD_NURTURE_ENABLED both exist in the Production env (via allowed 'vercel env ls'), predating the current deployment, so the 15:22/15:25Z 401s were external probes, not rejected cron traffic.

Decisive new evidence: I watched prod runtime logs across the next hour boundary. At 16:00:41Z the current production deployment (property-tax-partners-nfr50cmkr) logged 'GET /api/cron/lead-nurture -> 200' — an authenticated (CRON_SECRET-bearing, hence 200 not 401) Vercel cron invocation at precisely the scheduled slot. This is the exact verification the finding requested, and it passes. The impact scenario ('leads never advance past step 0/1') is therefore disproven for the current state.

Two residual notes worth carrying as info (not new medium findings): (1) the finding's suggested fallback check 'confirm the 07:00 digest arrives tomorrow' is unreliable — Property\web\src\lib\leads\nurture-digest.ts returns {sent:false} on no-activity days, so a missing digest email is NOT evidence of cron failure; (2) there is no heartbeat/last-run channel anywhere (docs\property\LEAD_NURTURE_OBSERVABILITY.md has none), and the stuck_leads guardrail runs INSIDE the same cron, so a future cron-scheduling failure would be silent until a lead visibly stalls. That design observation is adjacent to known-open item 1 (alert-only posture) and is the only enduring content of this finding.

Verdict: the finding was honest and factually accurate at audit close (hence is_real=true, not a fabrication), but with invocation now positively evidenced it is a resolved verification item, severity info.

confirmed.title: Quiet hours are enforced only at scheduling time, not at send time: a cron backlog or a pause/resume dumps SMS outside the window (including Sundays)
confirmed.location: packages/web-shared/lead-nurture/cron.ts:61-68 + send.ts:98-136 (no window recheck) vs. Property/web/src/lib/leads/aux-cron.ts:317,413 (which do recheck)
confirmed.claim: computeNextSendMs clamps next_action_at into the London window (email 08:00-20:30, SMS 09:00-20:30 Mon-Fri, Sat 10:00-18:00, never Sunday) at the moment the PREVIOUS step completes, but the cron fires anything with next_action_at <= now with no inSendWindow() check at dispatch, and the ChannelSender sends unconditionally. verdicts.reasoning: Verified end-to-end in code. findings.title: Nobody monitors the monitors: dead cron is indistinguishable from a quiet day, and guardrail alerts fate-share both the monitored channel (Resend) and the monitored cron
findings.claim: The observability layer has no external heartbeat or dead-man's switch. (1) The daily digest is deliberately 'quiet on dormant days', so the operator cannot distinguish 'healthy quiet day' from 'digest cron dead' (CRON_SECRET rotation, cron deregistration, deploy regression all fail silent). (2) Guardrail alerts run INSIDE the hourly lead-nurture cron they are supposed to watch — if the cron stops firing, alerting stops with it. (3) The only alert transport is Resend email (`getResend().emails.send`, failure only console.error'd): if Resend itself is the failing component (key revoked, account limit, suspension — precisely what drives failed_send_rate/bounce breaches), the alert about the failure also fails; the SMS channel exists in the stack but is never used for operator alerts. The prod auditor already could not positively prove the hourly cron executes; no auditor asked who would notice if it never does.
findings.evidence: digest route header: 'Quiet on dormant days (no sends, no stuck, no failures) so the operator inbox stays clean'. nurture-health.ts:350-361: alert sent solely via getResend(); catch -> console.error only. cron/lead-nurture/route.ts:75-85: runNurtureGuardrails called only inside this cron. Repo/docs contain no uptime monitor, heartbeat ping, or 'expected daily email' checklist (LEAD_NURTURE_OBSERVABILITY.md has no cron-liveness item). Prod auditor: 'hourly cron EXECUTION ... not yet positively proven to fire'.
findings.impact: The most likely total-failure modes (cron silently stops; Resend account breaks) produce zero signal by design. Leads would quietly stop being nurtured/promoted — the exact 3-of-9 contactability problem the system was built to fix — for days before anyone noticed, and the owner would believe the green go-live state still held.

findings.title: The 2am rollback path is worse than known-open item 3 describes: the ONLY documented no-redeploy pause control is a console button that is not deployed, and no SQL fallback is documented

It is materially worse: the docs' stated requirement (4) is 'be able to pause the whole system without a redeploy', and the only operator-facing mechanism given is 'use the console Pause/Resume button (or resumeNurture)' — but the console deployment that carries that button and its /api/nurture-control route is not live. The kill switch also fails open on read errors (compliance low finding), so a paused state cannot even be confirmed from behaviour.

findings.title: /api/leads/generate-sequence reuses the token-signing master secret as a plain bearer header with a non-timing-safe comparison
findings.claim: The internal fire-and-forget endpoint authenticates with `token !== secret` (not crypto.timingSafeEqual, unlike every other route in the system) and the shared secret it compares against is LEAD_NURTURE_TOKEN_SECRET — the same secret that signs every booking/confirm/opt-out token for every lead. The submit route ships that master secret over a public-internet fetch in an x-internal-token header to the site's own URL. Any header-logging middleware, proxy log, or future misconfiguration that captures request headers exposes the secret that can mint valid confirm tokens (false 'contactable' promotion + DJH handoff) or opt-out tokens (silent lead kill) for arbitrary lead ids. Route is currently unreachable in practice (copyAiEnabled off), so this is latent hardening debt no auditor recorded.
findings.evidence: generate-sequence/route.ts:26: `if (!secret || token !== secret) { return ... 401 }` — plain string comparison. route header comment: 'Security: a shared-secret header check (x-internal-token) guards the route.' submit/route.ts:254: `const internalToken = process.env.LEAD_NURTURE_TOKEN_SECRET ?? "";` sent via fetch headers.
findings.impact: If the AI copy layer is ever armed, the highest-value secret in the system (it forges the exact GET side effects two auditors rated high) starts transiting as a reusable static header; a single leaked log line compromises the integrity of the entire contactability gate. Cheap fix: dedicated internal secret + timingSafeEqual.

completeness.summary: Completeness critique of the 7-auditor audit, all checks read-only. The auditors were thorough inside their lanes but missed the system's edges. Biggest miss (GAP-1): a THIRD cron, /api/nurture/send (the old subscriber marketing drip), arms itself on Boolean(CRON_SECRET) — the lead-nurture go-live env changes silently un-parked it; it sits outside the kill switch, guardrails, digest and send log, shares the sending domain's reputation, has a disjoint opt-out store, and its subscribe form is live on every blog post (currently latent: 1 paused subscriber, 0 sends, verified in prod). Second (GAP-2): four routes in the audit's own named scope (notify, enrich, sync, ics) were covered by nobody; probing them found the AI+CH enrichment pipeline armed in prod (trigger installed, health GET green) yet with ZERO lead_enrichment rows ever — the promised 'enriched dossier' is silently hollow, the failure is undetectable by design, and the path is an un-flag-gated AI processor of lead text that the compliance 'AI dead-off' verdict holds against only by accident. Structural gaps: no dead-man's switch anywhere — a dead cron is indistinguishable from a quiet day and guardrail alerts run inside the monitored cron and only via the monitored channel (GAP-3); the documented no-redeploy pause is a console button that is not deployed, with no SQL fallback runbook (GAP-4, worse than known-open 3's framing); the old per-INSERT 'forward-ready' notify email still lands at T0 for Property leads with no do-not-forward marker (GAP-5); DMARC p=none/no-rua/no-root-SPF, a finite £18.10 Twilio balance and unverified Resend limits are unowned (GAP-6); the all-time funnel permanently dilutes the 3-of-9 KPI with 47 pre-go-live leads (GAP-7); and the token-signing master secret doubles as a non-timing-safe internal bearer (GAP-8). Positively verified: the engine is Property-only with no estate cross-contamination, the preview/dev enrolment seam is closed (local env points at staging, no arm flags), the Sheets mirror is off, ICS is token-authed, Twilio is a funded Full account, DKIM alignment makes mail deliverable today, legacy leads don't touch the stuck view, and the handoff doc's open items are all genuinely closed.
